question: Should QQBot gateway receive payloads be capped at 1 MiB, or use a more compatibility-conservative fixed limit such as 16 MiB?
rationale: The ws default is unnecessarily broad, but neither the supplied QQ protocol contract nor authenticated production proof establishes that every legitimate event fits below 1 MiB.

options.title: Adopt 16 MiB
options.body: Use the merged Discord-style boundary to retain substantial resource hardening while reducing the chance of rejecting an undocumented large QQ event.

options.title: Keep 1 MiB
options.body: Accept the tighter boundary only with QQ-owner confirmation or production evidence covering the largest supported event classes.

options.title: Leave the default
options.body: Retain the dependency’s 100 MiB window and defer hardening until QQ publishes or maintainers establish a supported maximum.

recommendation.title: Adopt 16 MiB
recommendation.body: Use the merged Discord-style boundary to retain substantial resource hardening while reducing the chance of rejecting an undocumented large QQ event.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently changed and proved the exact QQBot WebSocket factory that must safely combine this cap with the handshake deadline.
